@@99801370 <h> Eye on effective water-management strategies <p> Due to population growth , climate change and the rise of water-intensive clean energy technologies , the gap between renewable water supply and demand is expected to reach 40 per cent by 2030 . <p> WITH extreme weather events such as drought or flooding becoming more common due to climate change , countries around the world are looking to innovative solutions for water management . <p> Water scarcity captured global headlines last summer , as Europe experienced its worst drought in 500 years and China 's Yangtze River reached record low levels , derailing hydropower operations . Elsewhere , widespread flooding affected Nigeria , India , Pakistan and other parts of the world . <p> Due to population growth , climate change and the rise of water-intensive clean energy technologies , the gap between renewable water supply and demand is expected to reach 40 per cent by 2030 , according to US investment bank Morgan Stanley . The UN estimates that drought could affect over three-quarters of the world 's population by 2050 . <p> However , progress is being made , with the percentage of the global population with access to @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ 74 per cent between 2016 and 2020 , and an estimated 107 million people gaining access in 2020 alone . <p> Thanks to new government strategies , public-private initiatives and improvements in monitoring technologies , emerging markets are modernising their water-management and distribution networks while working to limit waste , and conserve and augment existing sources . <p> Monitoring technologies <p> In water-constrained areas , reducing water loss -- also known as non-revenue water ( NRW ) -- is typically more cost-effective than supply augmentation . New technologies such as smart meters and sensor networks can help limit loss and mitigate potential contamination . <p> Smart meters offer an internet-of-things solution to NRW by monitoring water distribution and usage , helping to identify inefficiencies and instances of leakage and theft . Market analyst firm Transforma Insight estimates that 700m smart water meters will be deployed globally by 2030 . <p> Founded in 2017 , Egyptian start-up Pylon offers subscription-based smart metering as a service to water and energy companies in Egypt and the Philippines , with plans to expand in Africa and Southeast Asia . <p> The company , which @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , leverages smart-grid infrastructure to help its clients reduce water losses by an estimated 22 per cent , enough to serve 40 million people per day . <p> Sensors can also play an integral role in improving sanitation efforts by identifying potential contaminants . <p> US-based water monitoring technology company Virridy , for example , aims to use investment from a June 2022 US$5.5 million Series A funding round to develop water E-coli sensors . The company already operates a network of satellite-linked borehole water monitors to boost drought resilience in Ethiopia , Kenya , Nigeria , Rwanda , Sierra Leone and Uganda . <p> Outdated or insufficient infrastructure is a major driver of NRW , with emerging markets losing some 45 million cu metres daily to leakages from ageing distribution networks , according to the World Bank . <p> In 2022 Manila Water , the water services company responsible for the Philippine capital , reduced NRW to 12.7 per cent , well below the World Bank standard of 25 per cent and on a par with NRW levels in Japan and Western Europe . The company used a combination @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ networks with local stakeholders allowing for quick responses to leakages or theft . <p> In addition to limiting municipal NRW , addressing inefficiencies in irrigation systems is an important step towards ensuring global water security . With roughly 70 per cent of global water usage dedicated to agriculture , improved monitoring and more sustainable agriculture practices in emerging markets are helping to boost food security around the world . <p> Conservation strategies <p> Ensuring universal access to and sustainable management of clean water and sanitation by 2030 is the focus of UN Sustainable Development Goal ( SDG ) 6 . To help organise global efforts for sustainable water management into actionable commitments , the first UN Water Conference in 50 years was held in New York City in March 2023 . <p> On a national scale , a number of countries have prioritised management of water supplies in recent years , with both government plans and new financing arrangements seeking to ensure improved water access . <p> In December 2022 Vietnam 's prime minister approved a water resources planning scheme for 2021-2030 that includes the goals of reducing water loss @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ clean water access rates to 95 to 100 per cent for urban areas and 65 per cent for rural areas by 2025 . <p> Saudi Arabia , which has the world 's third-highest per capita water consumption behind the US and Canada , aims to reduce its usage by 43 per cent by the end of the decade , in line with Saudi Vision 2030 . <p> In early 2023 the Kingdom announced the tendering of six wastewater treatment projects under public-private partnership ( PPP ) schemes to help upgrade the country 's infrastructure and reduce NRW . <p> In order to improve water access , countries such as Saudi Arabia have invested in desalination plants , especially as the industry attempts to reduce its carbon footprint and commodify wastewater . <p> Financing is central to the success of water-management projects , with the OECD estimating costs of US$1 trillion per year , or 1.21 per cent of global GDP , to achieve SDG 6 . Beyond government expenditure , performance-based contracting offers a key financing opportunity , incentivising companies based on their record for reducing NRW . <p> Ho @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , which is at risk of flooding and freshwater scarcity -- has effectively utilised this contracting model to upgrade its water distribution and sanitation infrastructure , saving the city an estimated 122 million litres of water daily . <p> In March 2023 global investment company Metito and British International Investment , the UK 's development finance institution , announced the launch of the Africa Water Infrastructure Development platform , which aims to fund sustainable water projects across Africa and boost the continent 's overall water security . <p> The platform 's first asset , a 40,000-cu-metre-per-day bulk surface water treatment plant in Kigali , Rwanda , provides 25 per cent of the city 's potable water supply and is the first PPP-run plant in sub-Saharan Africa outside of South Africa .

This idea greatly influenced the framers of the U.S. Constitution , leading to the establishment of a system of checks and balances . By implementing this separation of powers , the Founding Fathers sought to safeguard against tyranny and ensure a government that operates in the best interests of the people . The discovery , scientists said , may shed light on predicting future climate changes on Earth . <p> The research findings have been published online in the science journal Nature on Thursday , the China Lunar Exploration Project ( CLEP ) said on its official WeChat account on Monday . <p> Among planets in the solar system , Mars is considered to be the most similar to Earth . " Therefore , the study of Martian climate evolution has long been a topic of great interest , and wind and sand activity have shaped the extensive distribution of sand dune features on the Martian surface . <p> " Wind and sand activities can be said to have recorded the characteristics of the late evolution and recent climate environment @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ climate change . This separation ensures a system of checks and balances , preventing any single branch from becoming too powerful . The executive branch , headed by the President , is responsible for enforcing laws and executing policies . Candidates compete to secure their party 's nomination and ultimately vie for the presidency . However , it is worth examining the role of the electoral college , an indirect voting system , in electing the President . This system allocates electoral votes to each state based on its representation in Congress , influencing the outcome of the election . Additionally , representation in Congress is maintained through the House of Representatives and the Senate . The House of Representatives , with its members proportionally based on each state 's population , provides a platform for local representation . Members of the House of Commons are elected by the public , and the House of Lords consists of appointed and hereditary members . A critical analysis of each system -- the US Electoral College and the UK 's First Past the Post ( FPTP ) -- reveals unique implications , strengths , and weaknesses that significantly impact their respective political landscapes . <p> The US Electoral College System and @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ and distinctive system used to elect the President of the United States . Under this system , voters do not directly elect the President ; instead , they cast their ballots for a group of electors who represent their state . The number of electors for each state is determined by its congressional delegation , combining the number of Senators ( always two ) and Representatives based on the state 's population . This creates a balance between the influence of smaller and larger states , ensuring that no single state dominates the election process . <p> However , the Electoral College system has significant implications , some of which have sparked debates and criticism : <p> Winner-Takes-All System : In most states , the candidate who wins the popular vote secures all of that state 's electoral votes , leaving no representation for the losing party . For example , voters in less populous states have proportionally more influence than voters in heavily populated states , as each state is guaranteed a minimum of three electoral votes regardless of its population size . <p> The UK 's First Past the Post ( FPTP ) System and Its Effects on Representation <p> In contrast to the US Electoral College , the UK employs the First Past the Post ( FPTP ) system to elect Members of Parliament ( MPs ) to the House of Commons . In each electoral constituency , the candidate with the most votes wins , regardless of whether they have an outright majority . While the FPTP system is straightforward and promotes decisive outcomes , it has its own set of effects on representation : <p> Single-Party Dominance : The @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ lead to single-party dominance in Parliament . This can result in a lack of proportional representation and potential disillusionment among voters who feel their voices are not adequately heard . <p> Safe Seats and Tactical Voting : Over time , certain constituencies become known as " safe seats , " where a particular party consistently wins by a significant margin . In such constituencies , voters from opposing parties may resort to " tactical voting " -- voting for a less preferred candidate who has a better chance of defeating the party they most wish to avoid . <p> Underrepresentation of Minority Parties : The FPTP system can limit the representation of smaller or regional parties , as they may struggle to win in individual constituencies . @@100313589 <p> WHO has heard or learned of this scientist ? One might cast one 's mind back to one 's schooldays when the Geography teacher mentioned the Humboldt Current -- a cold current flowing from the Southern Ocean northwards along the Chilean and Peruvian coasts or the Biology teacher may have talked about the Humboldt penguin found on the shores of Peru . <p> Alexander von Humboldt was born in Berlin in 1769 and lived to the ripe old age of 89 and buried in the city of his birthplace following a Prussian state funeral . He was born into a wealthy military family with state connections and educated at home by two prominent tutors , Hertz , a physician and Willenow who later became one of the world 's greatest botanists . As a boy , he was forever collecting and labelling insects , plants , and shells which stood him in good stead for later life . At university -- he attended five -- his studies ranged from mineralogy , finance , and anatomy . <p> Wanderlust <p> It was on a visit to Mainz in 1789 when the 20-year-old Humboldt chanced to meet and befriend Georg @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Cook on his second expedition . It was on a journey to England with Forster later that year that they met up with Sir Joseph Banks , the then President of the Royal Society . Banks had also been on Cook 's expeditions . Their worldly accounts of expedition work no doubt fuelled Humboldt 's desire to explore but financing such thoughts was another matter ! <p> With a Diploma from the Freiberg School of Mines in 1792 , he was appointed to the Department of Mines as an inspector . There he excelled not only in increasing gold production but also in his genuine concern for miners ' welfare . He opened a school for the miners and paid for it out of his own pocket as well as establishing an emergency relief fund for accident prone miners . It was near these mines that he spent his free time studying the local vegetation and published his first biological work . This caught the eye of Goethe with whom he established a friendship . His fascination with botany led him to Italy and Switzerland . <p> Overseas expeditions <p> @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ 1799 to request authorisation from King Charles IV of Spain to form an expedition , at his own expense , to visit Spanish held territories in Central and South America for the next five years . He visited Venezuela , Cuba , Colombia , Peru , and Ecuador and was accompanied by Aime Bonpland , a renowned botanist and the expedition 's doctor . <p> In Venezuela he explored the Orinoco River almost to its source in Portuguese held Brazil . There , in a valley , he noticed how the forest was being cleared for the development of cocoa plantations supplying the world 's chocolate trade and he hit upon the idea of human-induced climate change . <p> There was a rapid fall in the water level in the valley 's Lake Valencia which Humboldt attributed to deforestation and the inability of exposed soils to retain water . With the trees removed the soils were deprived of shade and exposed to increased radiation and thus evaporation . His diary notes recorded , " man 's mischief " in disturbing " nature 's order " . He certainly possessed an @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ river that he documented the lifestyles of several native tribes and discovered electric eels . <p> Treks in Cuba <p> Whilst there he studied the agricultural output of sugar cane and carried out mineralogical surveys . An avid plant collector and no mean artist , his beautiful illustrations of species alerted the western world as to what lay beyond . <p> Andean expeditions ( 1801 to 1803 ) <p> Sailing to northern South America led to his arrival in Colombia and he soon moved to Bogota followed by a long trek across the snow-covered ranges of the Andes mountains to Quito in Ecuador . In 1802 , he climbed more than 5,878 metres up the side of Mount Chimborazo in Ecuador , setting a mountaineering record for a western climber . He knew the exact height for he had devised a type of altimeter -- such was his ingenuity , and he was at 300 metres below the summit of this volcano . It was during this expedition that he gained an insight into the interconnections of the living and the physical world . <p> Based on sketches he made @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ 's climatic and ecological altitudinal zones noting the heights where agriculture ceased , and the permanent snowline began . From this particular expedition , he has been accredited with the title as ' Father of Biogeography ' . <p> In 2012 , a research team retraced Humboldt 's steps up the mountain and produced a similar diagram of zones and the present-day ecological zones and the changes as shown in the accompanying juxtaposed diagram . Clearly , dramatic ecological shifts affected by climate change together with improved farming methods can be seen and particularly in the revised height of the snowline . <p> Later , in Peru , he studied the rich nitrogen properties of guano ( accumulated bat and bird droppings ) and the publication of his findings prompted an export trade in these fertilisers to Europe , which continues to this very day . It was on his one-year visit to Mexico from 1803 that he produced a vast number of altimetric readings and other recorded data which he described as " the basis of all scientific understandings " . His obsession with quantification became known as ' @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ in 1817 that he developed the idea of isothermal ( equal temperature ) lines drawn on maps thus comparing the climates of different countries and much later to be used by German climatologists in producing world climatic zone maps . He investigated the rate of temperature decrease with an increase in altitude thereby explaining convectional tropical storms . He noted that volcanoes fell naturally into linear chains related to their vast cavernous magma chambers underground . <p> It was in early 1857 , living in Berlin , that he suffered a stroke but hung on until May 1859 . His dying words were , " How glorious these sunbeams are ! They seem to call Earth to the Heavens ! " <p> He had many honours bestowed on him by distinguished scientific societies worldwide in his lifetime , but he was more chuffed by the way , as a scientific traveller , he had inspired others to follow in his wake . Amongst these was Charles Darwin , who admitted that his voyage in HMS Beagle was inspired by Humboldt 's travels and writings . He declared , " Humboldt @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ " <p> Interestingly , Alfred Russel Wallace made no mention of Humboldt in his writings other than in a meeting with a friend who had visited Humboldt Bay in Papua New Guinea . Undoubtedly , Humboldt , had he been alive , would have acknowledged Wallace 's findings in ' The Malay Archipelago ' first published 10 years after Humboldt 's death . <p> The importance of Humboldt today may be measured in terms of 14 geographical features , 19 species of birds , plants , insects , animals , and fish and over 16 places bearing the name Humboldt , and especially the Alejandro de Humboldt National Park in Cuba . His influence on the ecological , biogeographical , climatological , and cartographical areas of scientific research still lingers on 164 years after his death . He was , indeed , a most extraordinary traveller .

Firstly , it may lead to a " bandwagon effect " where voters gravitate towards perceived frontrunners , influencing their choices rather than evaluating policy positions . Secondly , excessive attention on polls can overshadow substantive issues and policy discussions , reducing the quality of political discourse . Thirdly , polls may be subject to sampling biases and methodological limitations , potentially leading to inaccurate predictions and misrepresentation of public sentiment . Fourthly , continuous poll reporting can create a horse race narrative , emphasizing competition over comprehensive policy analysis . To address these issues , media outlets should balance poll coverage with in-depth reporting on candidates ' platforms , fostering a more informed electorate and a healthier democratic process .

The United States ' political @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ the resilience and adaptability of the Pluralist Theory . <h> Criticisms of Pluralist Theory <p> Source : rsu <p> Pluralist Theory faces critiques regarding its recognition of diverse interest groups while potentially overlooking elitist influence and differential access to policymakers . Critics argue that powerful actors may wield disproportionate control , marginalizing smaller groups . Proponents defend Pluralism , highlighting open competition and incremental policy change . Through a more in-depth understanding of the interaction between migration and politics , the country can better manage the rapidly changing landscape and seize opportunities that arise . <p> Internal migration 's impact on American politics is a very important topic that deserves serious attention and thought from policymakers , researchers , and citizens alike . The United States must recognize and embrace the transformative power of internal migration if it is to navigate the 21st century political arena with resilience and unity .
